step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage CMOS operational amplifier configured as a unity-gain voltage follower with Miller compensation and zero-nulling resistor
step1_figure.description: Figure 24.14 (page 782) shows the closed-loop voltage follower configuration of the op-amp with compensation capacitor Cc = 2.4 pF, zero-nulling resistor Rz = 6.5 kΩ, and load capacitance CL = 100 fF. The underlying op-amp transistor topology with cascode current biases and Rz-Cc compensation network is detailed in Figure 24.8 (page 778).

unity_gain_frequency.description: Unity-gain frequency (gain-bandwidth product) of the op-amp determined by input transconductance and compensation capacitor

equation.explanation: The gain-bandwidth product where open-loop gain drops to unity, set by the input stage transconductance gm1 and compensation capacitance Cc.
equation.assumptions: Single dominant-pole approximation holds; Cc >> parasitic capacitances.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Itail ≈ 20 uA (10 uA per branch M1/M2), assuming W/L ≈ 10/0.5: gm1 = sqrt(2 * un*Cox * (W/L) * ID1) = sqrt(2 * 270e-6 * 20 * 10e-6) ≈ 328 uA/V (or for lower W/L ~150 uA/V as in textbook). Using gm1 ≈ 150 uA/V and Cc = 2.4 pF: fun = 150e-6 / (2 * pi * 2.4e-12) ≈ 9.95 MHz ≈ 10 MHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard biasing yields gm1 in the range 100–300 uA/V, giving unity gain frequency around 7–20 MHz with Cc = 2.4 pF.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the loop gain, measured as 180 degrees plus the phase of AOL at unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Margin against oscillation when AOL crosses 0 dB. With Rz = 1/gm2 nulling the RHP zero, the phase response exhibits first-order roll-off with ~90° phase lag at fun.
equation.assumptions: Rz correctly placed and tuned to 1/gm2 = 6.5 kΩ; non-dominant pole f2 >> fun.

sky130_expected.calculation: At fun ≈ 10 MHz, dominant pole f1 ≈ 287 kHz contributes -90°, the nulled zero contributes 0°, and second pole f2 > 100 MHz contributes -arctan(10/100) ≈ -6°. PM = 180° - 90° - 6° ≈ 84°–90°.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The 6.5 kΩ nulling resistor cancels the RHP zero, ensuring an overdamped/critically-damped response with PM near 90°.

gain_margin.description: Gain margin of the amplifier, measured as the attenuation (negative dB gain) when phase reaches -180 degrees

equation.explanation: The gain below unity (in dB) when the loop phase shift equals -180 degrees.
equation.assumptions: High-frequency poles cause phase to cross -180 degrees.

sky130_expected.calculation: As shown in Fig 24.13, when phase crosses -180°, the gain is around -25 dB, providing GM ≈ 25 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High second-pole frequency combined with zero-nulling resistor ensures adequate attenuation prior to -180° phase crossover.

open_loop_dc_gain.description: Low-frequency differential open-loop voltage gain of the two-stage op-amp

equation.explanation: Total DC gain is the product of first stage differential gain (gm1*R1) and second stage common-source gain (gm2*R2).
equation.assumptions: All transistors operate in saturation region.

sky130_expected.calculation: With gm1 ≈ 150 uA/V, ro1 ≈ 1/(lambda*ID1) = 1/(0.1*10u) = 1 MOhm, R1 ≈ 500 kOhm -> A1 ≈ 75 (37.5 dB). Second stage gm2 ≈ 150 uA/V, R2 ≈ 500 kOhm -> A2 ≈ 75 (37.5 dB). Total DC gain AOL = 75 * 75 ≈ 5625 ≈ 75 dB (typically 60 to 75 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Two common-source/diff stages in 130nm standard CMOS typically yield 30–35 dB gain per stage.

dominant_pole_frequency.description: Frequency of the dominant pole created by Miller multiplication of Cc across the second stage

equation.explanation: Miller effect magnifies Cc at node 1 by the second-stage gain gm2*R2.
equation.assumptions: Cc dominates over C1 and Cgd of M7.

sky130_expected.calculation: With gm2 = 150 uA/V, R1 = 111 kOhm, R2 = 333 kOhm, Cc = 2.4 pF: f1 ≈ 1 / (2 * pi * 150e-6 * 111e3 * 333e3 * 2.4e-12) ≈ 11.9 kHz (for Cc = 100 fF, f1 = 287 kHz; scaling to 2.4 pF gives ~12 kHz).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Large compensation capacitor (2.4 pF) pushes the dominant pole down into the tens of kHz range.

power_dissipation.description: Total quiescent power consumed by the op-amp core and biasing

equation.explanation: Product of supply voltage VDD and sum of all branch currents (diff pair tail current, second stage current, and bias generator current).
equation.assumptions: Circuit is in quiescent operating point with inputs at mid-rail.

sky130_expected.calculation: VDD = 1.8 V. Op-amp core currents: IM6 ≈ 20 uA, IM8 ≈ 10 uA. Bias circuit adds ~30 uA. Total current Itot ≈ 60 uA. P = 1.8 V * 60 uA = 108 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Tail currents are set in the 10-20 uA range, with 1.8V VDD in sky130.

output_swing_high.description: Maximum output voltage before the PMOS driver enters triode region

equation.explanation: Limited by the saturation voltage of output PMOS transistor M7.

sky130_expected.calculation: VDD = 1.8 V. For PMOS sourcing ~10 uA, Vdsat_M7 ≈ 100 mV to 150 mV. Vout_max = 1.8 - 0.15 = 1.65 V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Overdrive voltage for M7 is kept near 100-150 mV for high swing.

output_swing_low.description: Minimum output voltage before the NMOS cascode current sink enters triode region

equation.explanation: Limited by the sum of drain-source saturation voltages across cascode current sink transistors M8T and M8B.
equation.assumptions: Both M8T and M8B remain in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Each NMOS has Vdsat ≈ 100 mV. Vout_min = 2 * 100 mV ≈ 200 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Cascode stack requires roughly 2 * Vdsat headroom from ground.

slew_rate.description: Slew rate of the amplifier under large-signal step conditions

equation.explanation: Rate of change of the output voltage when the differential pair is completely steered, charging/discharging compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Output current capability does not limit before Cc charging current.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Itail = 20 uA and Cc = 2.4 pF: SR = 20 uA / 2.4 pF = 8.33 V/us.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Tail current of 20 uA charging 2.4 pF gives ~8.3 V/us.

small_signal_rise_time.description: 10% to 90% rise time in response to a small input step (5 mV), exhibiting first-order settling

equation.explanation: For a first-order response with PM ≈ 90°, the closed-loop system behaves like an RC filter with tau = 1/(2*pi*fun) = Cc / gm1.
equation.assumptions: Step is small enough (5 mV) to avoid slew rate limiting.

sky130_expected.calculation: tau = 2.4 pF / 150 uA/V = 16 ns. tr = 2.2 * 16 ns ≈ 35 ns.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Smooth first-order step response as depicted in Figure 24.14.

step3_testbench.description: Complete ngspice testbench for the two-stage op-amp voltage follower verifying DC operating point/power, AC closed-loop bandwidth and stability metrics, and transient small-signal and large-signal step responses.
